claims.text: Combining in situ high-temperature XRD with TGA enables simultaneous measurement of phase transformations and oxidation kinetics in high-entropy alloys.
The combined method provides a direct link between oxidation behaviour and phase stability.
CrCoFeMnNi can be prepared in a single-phase as-cast or annealed microstructure for the proposed experiment.
The alloy should be exposed to temperatures above 1000°C during in situ XRD and TGA measurements.
A controlled oxygen partial-pressure environment can be used during the high-temperature measurements.
Temperatures above 1000°C and controlled oxygen atmospheres replicate high-temperature service conditions.
In situ high-temperature XRD can reveal time- and temperature-dependent phase evolution during oxidation of CrMnFeCoNi.
XRD can detect the onset and identity of oxide-phase formation during high-temperature oxidation.
High-temperature oxidation may transform a single-phase solid solution into a multiphase structure.
TGA mass changes measured alongside XRD represent oxidation behaviour.
The integrated XRD-TGA technique directly correlates oxidation-induced mass changes with phase-transformation dynamics.
Continuous diffraction-pattern monitoring and simultaneous weight-gain measurement can temporally align phase transformations with oxidation events.
Oxidation reactions that produce crystal-structure changes can be tracked by in situ high-temperature XRD.
Changes in XRD patterns will indicate oxide formation or structural decomposition.
TGA weight gain will quantify oxidation kinetics.
Concurrent XRD changes and TGA weight gain would demonstrate the method's ability to link oxidation behaviour with phase stability.
Traditional methods assess oxidation kinetics and phase stability separately under simplified conditions.
Transient phase changes faster than the measurement resolution may not be detected.
Alloy-specific oxidation responses may affect the detection limits and applicability of the method.
Validation across additional high-entropy-alloy compositions is required.
